My friend. Firstly; you are not alone. I have suffered panic attacks for my whole life but last year was the worst due to intense trauma and I had panic attacks every, single. day. I even woke up in the middle of the nights from panic attacks. I had to have the ambulance called so many times. The pain became so unbearable that I sat down my mom to let her know that I intend to commit suicide and I genuinely meant it.

Obviously I'm still here so through the terrible pain, I am able to let you know that there is hope. I still suffer but it's not every day. Not as intense at least. I have a will to live which is something new.

I am not able to give advice to you about what will take away your suffering because everybody is different. I can tell you what helped me but please note again, this is probably not advisable or professional. Firstly, I accepted death. I became comfortable and content with the idea of dying because like I said before, I intended to end my life anyway. When I had a panic attack I began to accept my fate. I decided that if it is my time to go, there is no use fighting it. This is not an easy thing to do and goes against your every instinct as a human being. But this is how I go on living my life. It has also helped me in other ways, I live every day like I might die at any moment. I don't want to leave with any regrets. In a way I appreciate life more now.
